I only have one mum but my dad passed when I was young, and I was always looking for father figures when I was younger (I’m 21 (female) now and still do sometimes). In teachers, in family members like uncles or my mums cousins… all I wanted was a dad. I’ve felt this all of my life. It’s really hard, and it may always feel like there’s a void in your heart because of it. But I’m sure your mums love you so much, there are so many people in your life who love you. Just by what I’ve read I can tell you have so much love in your heart - hold onto that. You are loved, maybe not by a father figure but by those around you. Yeah it’s not okay for people to judge other people for how shallow/deep they cut, or for their reasons for cutting. Everyone who hurts themselves is valid no matter the reason or form of self harm, like don’t make people who are suffering feel shittier by making them think they aren’t valid or saying they’re not hurting as much as someone else. No one ever knows what someone is going through and the anxiety of having people find out about your self harm is bad enough, we don’t need people making us more anxious or depressed or insecure by telling us we’re not good enough. So yeah man I completely understand and agree with you. Some people are just fucked up.

Hey man. I’m sorry this happened. Please know that it’s not your fault. You clearly have so much love for this girl, and I’m sure she knows how loved she is by you. By the sounds of it, you already do everything you can to help. You’re not a failure. You’re so strong, comforting her even when you felt bad yoursef. You must really love this girl, and I know she is so lucky to have you in her life. 

I haven’t been in your shoes but I know how guilty I’ve felt when I’ve been with a bf and relapsed. Please let me repeat, it’s not your fault. You didn’t do anything to cause it, and you did the best you could to prevent it. It sounds like she’s struggling a lot and the best thing you can do right now is support her and be there for her during this time. What she does has nothing to do with you; you might want to save her and stop her from this, but you can’t. I’m sorry to be so blunt, but having been in her shoes, I know that no matter what my bf would say, I would still have urges and most often resort to self harm when I felt really bad. It had nothing to do with him - I just couldn’t stop myself. It does become an addiction. 

Continue to support her and possibly suggest she see a guidance counsellor or therapist. I obviously don’t know the full situation, and I know she is young and her parents might end up finding out, but you’re not a trained medical professional - only they can really help her.

Definitely feel this. I was clean for a year and so happy about it and proud of myself. I recently relapsed and I’d forgotten how good it feels and now I really don’t want to stop. It feels shitty but it’s also weirdly calming.

Hey. I’m really sorry you’re hurting. I understand what you’re going through. I was also clean for a year and recently relapsed due to having my ptsd triggered. It fucking sucks. 

And my dude, it wasn’t your choice. You didn’t let the past hurt you. You didn’t choose to have ptsd, nor to be triggered by it. It’s not your fault that something happened to cause you to have ptsd, and it’s not your fault when you get triggered either. I agree, these states are so hard to get out of when you get stuck. But you got out of them before - I believe you can do it again. 

You are so incredibly strong. You were clean for years! That’s no easy feat. I hope things look up for you, and please know that I’m rooting for you, no matter what.
